chunks: Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī wrote to Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī, peace be upon him:

Is it permissible that, for what is due regarding cultivated produce of wheat and barley, and what is due upon gold, dirhams be paid according to its equivalent value, or is it not permissible except that it be paid from each thing itself?
So he, peace be upon him, replied: “Whichever is easier may be given.”

key_terms.الذَّهَبِ: gold upon which zakat is due
key_terms.الْحَرْثِ: cultivated produce or crops subject to zakat
key_terms.تَيَسَّرَ: that which is easier or more feasible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay zakat in cash instead of giving it from the actual goods?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on paying zakat due on agricultural produce and gold by monetary value rather than strictly in kind. Imam Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام replies that whichever form is easier may be paid, indicating permissibility in giving the equivalent value.
